name: Alignment and Safety
strandNote: Optional on every quant track. For AI research roles, and for anyone who deploys a model that optimises a measured target.
description: See an agent game its reward and fix it, measure dangerous capabilities with honest statistics, and study how a weaker overseer can check a stronger system.

requires.why: Trains the gaming agent with the tabular Q-learning and gridworld of rl level 3.
Over-optimises a reward model with best-of-n and a KL penalty, from post-train level 2.
Builds on evaluation as statistics: standard errors, paired comparisons and contamination.
Builds on constitutional AI and AI feedback, taught in post-train level 3, without reteaching them.
Audits a model with the ablation and patching methods of interp level 4.

lessonNames.l2-an-agent-that-games: An agent that games its reward

lessonObjectives.l1-what-you-asked-for: Name the gap between the reward written down and the outcome wanted, in examples of specification gaming.
lessonObjectives.l2-an-agent-that-games: Show by value iteration and Q-learning that a gridworld agent loops on a respawning reward.
lessonObjectives.l3-fixing-the-reward: Design a potential-based shaping reward for the gridworld and check that the optimal policy reaches the goal.
lessonObjectives.l4-over-optimisation: Simulate best-of-n against a proxy reward and find where the true reward starts to fall.
lessonObjectives.l5-measuring-a-capability: Implement the unbiased pass@k estimator and say what an elicitation gap does to a capability claim.
lessonObjectives.l6-red-teaming: Report an attack success rate with an interval, including the bound when no attack succeeds.
lessonObjectives.l7-thresholds-and-policies: Decide whether a model is below a capability threshold using a one-sided bound and a safety margin.
lessonObjectives.l8-when-evaluations-fail: Explain how sandbagging, contamination and weak elicitation make an evaluation say too little.
lessonObjectives.l9-the-oversight-gap: Explain why human feedback stops working when the system is more capable than its supervisor.
lessonObjectives.l10-debate: Show how a debate lets a judge check a long claim by inspecting one step.
lessonObjectives.l11-weak-to-strong: Build a weak-to-strong experiment and compute the performance gap recovered.
lessonObjectives.l12-auditing-with-interpretability: Find a planted trigger in a small model by ablation and patching, as in an auditing game.
